senses.head: Of food or drink: small, easy to digest, or low in fat, calories or alcohol

senses.head: Of sleep: easily broken; of a sleeper: waking easily
examples: I'm a light sleeper, so the dog wakes me up.

senses.head: Having too little of something — in light on
examples: The report is light on details.

entries.position: both — a light bag, The bag is light; light on only after a verb
entries.takes: on + noun — having too little of something: light on details
entries.contrast: Light covers two unrelated ideas: 'not heavy' (лёгкий) and 'not dark' (светлый). But Russian лёгкий meaning 'not difficult' is easy: an easy test, not a light test. A light sleeper wakes easily (чутко спит). Lite is a spelling used on food labels (lite beer). Light on your feet means moving easily and gracefully, not 'lacking' like light on details. Travel light and sleep light use the adverb, and a lighter is a noun (зажигалка).

entries.position: both — a bright light, The light is bright
entries.contrast: A bright person is smart (умный, способный), not яркий: Russian яркая личность is a colorful personality or a striking person. A bright idea is often sarcastic. After verbs like shine, careful writing uses the adverb brightly, although shine bright is common in songs and speech.

entries.position: both — a round table, The table is round
entries.contrast: Russian круглый in set phrases is not round: круглый год is all year round (an adverb), круглые сутки is around the clock, круглый отличник is a straight-A student. A round-trip ticket (туда и обратно) is a compound adjective. Round as a preposition (round the corner) is British; Americans say around. A round (noun) is a раунд or a round of drinks.

senses.head: Old-fashioned and boring — dated slang
examples: My parents were so square in the '80s.

entries.position: both — a square box, The box is square; after a measurement for each side: ten feet square
entries.comparison: -er/-est or more/most — squarer, squarest, more square
entries.contrast: Word order changes the meaning: 100 square feet is an area, but a room ten feet square measures ten feet on each side (100 square feet in all). Square also means 'even, owing nothing' (We're square = мы в расчёте). A square (noun) is a площадь in a city: Times Square. More square is as common as squarer.

entries.meaning: Shaped like an egg or a stretched circle. ---
examples: An oval mirror hung over the sink.
The track around the field is oval.
Her face is more oval than round.
entries.position: both — an oval mirror, The mirror is oval
entries.contrast: Oval is both the adjective (овальный) and the noun (овал), so no ending changes: an oval table, shaped like an oval. The Oval Office is the president's office in the White House.

senses.head: Shaped like a triangle
examples: Yield signs in the US are triangular.
Cut the sandwiches into triangular pieces.
The park sits on a small triangular lot.

senses.head: Involving three people, groups or places
examples: The novel is about a triangular relationship between two sisters and one man.
Triangular trade linked Europe, Africa and the Americas.

entries.position: both — a triangular sign, The sign is triangular; the 'three parties' sense only before a noun
entries.contrast: Triangular sounds a little formal; in casual speech Americans often say triangle-shaped or use the noun: Cut it into triangles. A triangular relationship is what everyday English calls a love triangle (любовный треугольник).

entries.meaning: Shaped like a rectangle: four straight sides and four right angles, usually with two sides longer. ---
examples: We need a rectangular table that seats eight.
The pool in the backyard is rectangular.
Most phone screens are rectangular with rounded corners.
entries.position: both — a rectangular table, The table is rectangular
entries.contrast: False friend: rectangular describes only four-sided shapes. Russian прямоугольный треугольник is a right triangle in American English (right-angled triangle in British), and прямой угол is a right angle.

senses.head: Shaped like a circle
examples: The church has a large circular window over the door.

senses.head: Moving in a circle, or ending where it began
examples: There's a circular trail around the lake.

senses.head: Of an argument: using what it wants to prove as its proof
examples: That's circular reasoning, and it won't convince anyone.
Her argument is circular: the book is true because the book says so.

entries.position: both — a circular window, The window is circular
entries.contrast: In everyday speech Americans say round for most objects (a round table); circular sounds more formal or technical and suits flat shapes, routes and movement. Circular reasoning is рассуждение по кругу. A circular (noun) is a printed ad or flyer.

entries.meaning: Bent in a smooth line, not straight. ---
examples: The chef uses a knife with a curved blade.
The front of the building is curved like a wave.
This year's gaming monitors are more curved than last year's.
entries.position: both — a curved blade, The blade is curved
entries.contrast: Curved means bending smoothly (изогнутый). Russian кривой in the sense 'not straight as it should be' is crooked: a crooked picture, crooked teeth. Curvy means having many curves, like a mountain road, or describes a full, shapely figure.

senses.head: Made of wood
examples: We crossed an old wooden bridge over the creek.

entries.position: both — a wooden spoon, The floors are wooden
entries.comparison: more/most — only in the 'stiff' sense: more wooden, most wooden
entries.contrast: For the material, Americans use the noun as often as the adjective: wood floors and a wood table are as common as wooden floors. Only wooden has the figurative sense 'stiff, without expression': wooden acting, never wood acting.
